title: Master Protocol App
text:
Coming Soon
The IDSWG Master Protocol Working Group is developing an interactive application for exploring the landscape of master protocol clinical trials. The app will allow users to filter and analyze trials by design type, disease area, phase, sponsor, and status.
The app is not yet publicly available. This page will be updated with a link and embed once deployment is complete.
For methodology and design guidance, see the Resources page.

title: Master Protocol App
text:
Interested in Contributing?
The app is maintained by the Concept, Methodology and Framework Sub-team. If you have relevant expertise in Shiny development, data curation, or master protocol methodology and want to contribute, contact the IDSWG at asadahshuidswg@gmail.com or the IDSWG at asadahshuidswg@gmail.com.

title: Events & KOL Lectures
text:
KOL Lecture Series
The IDSWG KOL Lecture Series has been running since 2015. Each month the series invites key opinion leaders from academia, industry, and regulatory agencies to share insights on the methodology, application, and practical considerations of innovative clinical trial design.
Format: Monthly webinars, Fridays 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM EST
Attendance: 100 to 200 participants per session, open to all.
Join the meeting: Zoom link
Chairs (2025): Heng Zhou (Merck), Yi Pan (Bristol Myers Squibb)
Members: John Loewy (Data ForeThought), Xiaofei Bai (Moderna)
To present or nominate a speaker for 2026, contact any committee member.

Overview
The NEED Sub-team is co-led by Qi Zhang (Sanofi) and Daoyuan Shi (BlueRock Therapeutics). The sub-team works to ensure that evidence standards reflect what matters to patients and their families, not only what is statistically tractable.

title: Randomization Working Group Named PSI SIG of the Year
text:

The IDSWG Randomization Working Group has been named PSI Special Interest Group of the Year for 2025, a recognition of its sustained contributions to randomization methodology in clinical trials.
The Randomization WG is co-chaired by Johannes Krisam and Kerstine Carter (both Boehringer Ingelheim) and Alex Sverdlov (Novartis). The group currently has approximately 50 active and inactive members spanning pharmaceutical industry (19), academia (24), and other organizations (7), with representation across Europe/UK and the USA.
The WG’s work focuses on moving beyond standard permuted-block randomization to bring awareness of modern methodological advances in the field. Activities include monthly member meetings, open learning sessions, a dedicated website, and a growing library of publications, slide sets, and educational resources.
Congratulations to the Randomization WG team on this well-deserved recognition.

section: Why Patient Engagement Matters in Master Protocols
text:
Why Patient Engagement Matters in Master Protocols
Master protocol trials, particularly platform and basket designs, are operationally complex and can span years or decades. Ensuring that patients understand what they are enrolling in, that endpoints reflect outcomes meaningful to them, and that participation burden is minimized requires active patient engagement from the design stage onward.
Prior MPWG work has addressed patient engagement directly:

Overview
The ASA-DahShu IDSWG Master Protocol Working Group (MPWG) is a joint effort co-chaired by Cindy Lu (AstraZeneca) and Robert Beckman, M.D. (Georgetown University), operating under the American Statistical Association, DahShu IDSWG, and Bayesian Scientific Working Group umbrella.
The MPWG focuses on the methodology, regulatory landscape, and operational implementation of master protocols, covering basket, umbrella, and platform trials that evaluate multiple treatments or patient populations within a single overarching study framework.

About the Program
The StatBridge Future Leaders Program is an IDSWG initiative designed to support early-career biostatisticians and data scientists at the intersection of academic training and clinical practice. The program grew from a recognized gap: biostatisticians emerging from graduate programs often have strong methodological foundations but limited exposure to the practical realities of pharmaceutical drug development, regulatory interactions, and cross-functional team dynamics.
StatBridge addresses that gap through mentorship, structured exposure to IDSWG sub-team work, and professional development opportunities within a global community of quantitative scientists.
Program Co-Leads:

Bryan McComb, Ph.D., Associate Director of Biostatistics, Pfizer; Co-Leader of External Collaborations, IDSWG
Courtney Henry, Ph.D., GSK; Co-Leader of Community, IDSWG

title: StatBridge Future Leaders Program
text:
What We Offer

    Pairing with experienced biostatisticians from pharma, academia, and regulatory settings. Mentors offer career guidance, project feedback, and professional network introductions.

    Opportunities to observe and contribute to active IDSWG sub-teams, gaining experience in collaborative scientific work, publication processes, and regulatory engagement.

    Pathways to present at IDSWG events, including the annual meeting, KOL Lecture Series, and major conferences such as JSM and SCT.

title: StatBridge Future Leaders Program
text:
Who Should Join
The StatBridge program is designed for:

Graduate students in biostatistics, statistics, data science, or related quantitative fields who are interested in pharmaceutical or clinical research careers
Early-career biostatisticians (typically within the first five years post-PhD or MS) working in academia, industry, or government who want to deepen their exposure to innovative trial design
Academic researchers who collaborate with industry or regulatory bodies and want to strengthen those connections

There are no formal requirements for participation. The program is open to members from all geographic locations and institutional backgrounds. Students and early-career professionals with backgrounds in patient advocacy, health communications, or clinical research operations are also welcome, the program values diverse perspectives on what makes trial design work in practice.

How Sub-teams Work
Each sub-team is a volunteer working group centered on a specific methodological or operational topic. Participation is entirely flexible, members may observe, contribute, take a leadership role, or propose a new sub-team at any time. The Leadership Team provides mentorship and consultation to anyone starting or stepping into a leadership role.
The IDSWG actively welcomes members from across the public health and drug development spectrum, including statisticians, clinicians, pharmacometricians, regulators, epidemiologists, health economists, ethicists, patient advocates, and clinical operations professionals. This interdisciplinary mix participates as full members across sub-teams and brings the range of perspectives needed to make innovative trial designs rigorous, practical, and relevant to the people they are meant to serve.
To join a sub-team or propose a new one, contact Bob, Mercedeh, or Alex, contact details are on the About page.

Patient Engagement Sub-team
The Patient Engagement sub-team, previously led by Deborah Collyar of Patient Advocates in Research (PAIR), is currently seeking a new leader.
Patient engagement is not a peripheral activity for the IDSWG, it is embedded in the group’s mission. Innovative trial designs should reduce patient burden, reflect what patients actually care about measuring, and be accessible to the populations who most need them. The Patient Engagement Sub-team works at the intersection of trial methodology and patient advocacy, ensuring that design innovation serves patients rather than simply optimizing operational or statistical metrics.
Activities have included joint workshops with patient communities, consultation on endpoint selection for rare disease trials, and contributions to the NEED Sub-team’s work on evidence standards for rare diseases.
If you are interested in leading this sub-team, please contact Mercedeh Ghadessi (asadahshuidswg@gmail.com).
